Adding a new PSID wave

Source: ADDING_A_WAVE.md

Waves later than psid_latest_wave() are rejected by build.panel() by default. After importing the zips of a new wave with getPSID(), you can build it right away with build.panel(..., detect_waves = TRUE), which reads psid_waves_detected.csv (written by getPSID()) and uses the detected variable names with a warning. The checklist below stays the reference and the permanent route: it makes the wave work for everyone without detect_waves = TRUE. Detection does not update psid.xlsx, so the variable lists still have to be extended yourself with extendVarsPSID().

  1. R/makeids.r, makeids(): extend year; append ONE element to each of ind.interview, ind.seq, ind.head and fam.interview (names from the new IND and FAM codebooks, never guessed — the crosswalk can only suggest candidates such as ERxxxxx); extend the ind.head.num rep() count, and confirm the head code in the codebook (the label may have changed). This manual edit is the permanent route: once it is released, build.panel() supports the new wave without detect_waves = TRUE.

  2. psid_family_table() in R/makeids.r: extend year and append NA_integer_ to file.

  3. inst/psid-lists/: replace psid.xlsx with the latest official PSID cross-year workbook (PSID Data Center, “Cross-Year Index”; do not edit cells by hand), then run Rscript data-raw/update-varlists.R (dry run). Review the review table against the codebooks (definitions can change between waves; check every status other than added), and only then run Rscript data-raw/update-varlists.R write.

  4. Sample ranges: check whether new samples were added to the PSID sample definitions in build.panel() (SRC/SEO/immigrant/latino ranges in R/build.panel.r) and in the synthetic fixture testPSID() (R/makeids.r).

  5. devtools::test(): test-waves.R, test-wave-latest.R and test-psid-lists.R fail loudly if a vector has the wrong length, a name is duplicated or a list contains a year that is not supported; no test needs editing.

  6. Add a NEWS bullet.

  7. Never commit real PSID data; tests use synthetic fixtures only.
